einzeiler: Author Katherine Stockett discusses her 17-year literary return with The Calamity Club.
kurzfassung: Author Katherine Stockett joins the podcast to discuss her eagerly awaited second novel, The Calamity Club. Set in 1933 Mississippi, the sweeping narrative explores female survival, systemic oppression, and the haunting reality of historical eugenics laws. Stockett also reflects on her writing process, her creative partnership with editor Julie Grau, and the deep friendships that anchor her life in the South.
stichpunkte: Katherine Stockett returns with her second major novel, The Calamity Club, set in 1933 Mississippi.
The novel is told in two distinct voices: an 11-year-old girl in an orphanage and a resilient woman navigating the Mississippi Delta.
Stockett deliberately chose 1933 to examine historical injustices, including harsh sterilization and eugenics laws targeting women.
The story features a southern brothel not as a stereotype, but as a complex exploration of female agency and desperation.
The author spent 17 years researching, writing, and overcoming creative roadblocks before completing the book.
Stockett highlights the vital role of her editor, Julie Grau, in shaping the final manuscript.
The conversation explores recurring themes of exposing southern hypocrisy and the power of female solidarity.

clips.hook: A 1933 Mississippi setting full of systemic traps
clips.text: The author outlines how the main character faces escalating forms of discrimination and legal restrictions simply for being a woman in the 1930s.

clips.hook: The stark double standard surrounding virginity
clips.text: The discussion highlights how society viewed a young man visiting a brothel as a normal rite of passage while demanding absolute purity from brides.

clips.hook: When California's eugenics blueprint caught Hitler's eye
clips.text: The conversation reveals the shocking historical fact that aggressive American sterilization laws in California served as a direct model for Nazi Germany.

clips.hook: Financial independence was long out of reach for women
clips.text: The host points out that women could not obtain credit cards or business loans without a male cosigner until relatively recently in modern history.

clips.hook: John Grisham's advice on protecting creative energy
clips.text: The author shares how fellow writer John Grisham taught her to finally push back against relentless promotional tours in order to focus on writing.

beschreibung:
Thank you, dear listeners, for joining us this summer on You Are What You Read. We read your comments, and we know what books you have been reading and sharing with your book clubs. In the final weeks of summer, we are bringing back your favorite episodes and authors to the podcast. “The Best of Summer” on You Are What You Read welcomes back the biggest bestsellers of summer 2026. This week, Kathryn Stockett joins us with The Calamity Club.
